chunks: Whose punishment will be doubled on the Day of Judgement, and he will live for ever in disgrace,

key_terms.يَخْلُدْ: he will live forever / remain eternally

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for those whose punishment is doubled on the Day of Judgement?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (25:69-70) is often linked to the specific sin of *shirk* or major sins committed with arrogance, highlighting that the 'doubling' of punishment reflects both the severity of the act and the added humiliation of being cast out from divine mercy. The phrase 'humiliated' (*muhanan*) underscores the loss of dignity in the presence of Allah, a key theme in Al-Kulayni’s *Al-Kafi* when discussing the consequences of persistent sinners. This serves as a warning against not just the act itself, but the attitude of pride that accompanies it.
